title: Tauri migration: TypeScript Canonical Source foundation
description: Tauri v2/React/TypeScript desktop shellに、新規アプリデータ領域でCanonical SOURCEを保存・再読込する最小基盤を追加する。Python Vaultの既存データは開発プロトタイプとして移行対象外だが、既存データを自動削除・上書きしない。
design: Tauri official filesystem pluginを必要最小のcapability scopeで使う。React componentはraw invoke/plugin APIを直接呼ばず、TypeScript use case経由とする。filesystem/plugin/capability、storage、testsは一つの検証可能な変更に留め、R2はこの基盤に依存させる。
acceptance_criteria: TypeScript domainがSOURCE manifest/payloadの整合性を検証し、Tauri filesystem adapterはアプリ専用データ領域だけに限定される。first-runのみ空のCanonical layoutを初期化し、既存Canonicalを検出したら破壊せず停止する。capture -> close/reopen -> read/validate が実アプリで確認できる。SQLite/indexはCanonicalと別の派生物のままとする。
close_reason: TypeScript SOURCE integrity checks, app-local FS plugin storage, first-run safety, and TSUZU.app capture/reopen verification completed.

title: Tauri migration: canonical storage compatibility decision
description: 既存Python VaultのCanonical/derived形式を読み取りで棚卸しし、Tauri v2/TypeScript-first実装へ移す際の互換境界を確定する。既存データの書換え、ファイルシステム権限追加、R2のPython実装は行わない。
design: 新しいAGENTS.mdとIMPLEMENTATION_RULESに従う。永続形式を決める前にTauri filesystem/plugin/capabilityを追加しない。R2はこの判断の後にTypeScriptのingestion経路として再計画する。
acceptance_criteria: Canonical形式・派生形式・再構築可能なデータを区別して記録する。旧状態から新状態への移行に必要な最小のread-only fixtureとreopen確認計画を提示する。実データを引き継ぐか開発用として作り直すか、ユーザー判断が必要な一点を明記する。
notes:
読み取り棚卸し: Canonical SOURCE は canonical/sources/<UUIDv4>/source.md と payload/original。汎用Canonicalは canonical/objects/<TYPE>/<UUIDv4>/object.md と任意payload。system配下は staging/quarantine、deletion-ledger、各種receipt。control/active-vault.json はVault外のActive Vault locator。SQLite/FTSはVault外 index/tsuzu.sqlite の派生projectionで、reconcile/full_rebuildによりCanonicalから再構築可能。結論: Tauri移行ではこのディレクトリCanonical形式を不変のクロススタック契約として継承し、SQLiteをCanonicalに昇格させない。最小互換fixtureはSOURCE text/URL、SOURCE_VERSION、deletion ledgerを含め、old state -> TypeScript read/write -> close/reopen -> read/write を検証する。未決定: 現行Python Vaultを正式にサポートする既存データとして移行対象にするか、開発プロトタイプとして初期化可能にするか。
ユーザー判断（2026-09-14）: 現行Python Vaultは開発プロトタイプとして初期化可能。制約: 初期化は新規アプリデータ領域に限り、既存Vaultの自動削除・上書き・破壊的startup rewriteはしない。既存Canonicalを検出した場合は明示的に停止し、将来のimport/移行タスクで扱う。
close_reason: Canonical形式の棚卸しと初期化可能というユーザー判断を記録済み

title: Cross-surface ingress convergence: Codex and Tauri same Vault
description:
## Scope
Close the remaining cross-surface gap: Codex automatic capture and Tauri capture-draft ingress must resolve the same active Vault and converge on the same A3 CaptureService -> A4 SingleWriterWorker path.

## Current gap
The Codex hook still writes through AtomicSourceWriter directly and derives a project-hash root independently. That is not sufficient evidence for the canonical ownership contract even though Tauri ingress already uses A3/A4.

## Acceptance criteria
- Codex UserPromptSubmit resolves the shared Active Vault and submits a typed A3 request; it does not call a second Canonical writer directly.
- A Tauri draft and a Codex capture for the same configured project are materialized by one A4 writer into one Canonical Vault/index, with receipt/idempotency and secret guards preserved.
- Project isolation, retry/replay, disabled mode, and no-self-recall tests prove that cross-surface convergence does not leak data or create duplicate sources.
- ADR-008 and the desktop/Codex documentation state the same executable boundary.

## Verification
- Focused cross-surface Python tests plus the existing full Python suite.
- Tauri tests/build and a local draft -> Core receipt -> Codex recall smoke using one configured Vault root.
- Record the selected Vault-root migration behavior without rewriting existing user-owned Vaults.

## Dependencies
Existing C0, A3, A4, Codex hook, and Tauri ingress foundations above.

## Non-goals
No new Canonical store, no broad shell/network permission, no transcript scanning, and no Claude integration.
notes: 2026-09-23: Codex UserPromptSubmit now queues CODEX_USER_PROMPT through A3 and materializes only through the shared A4 worker; TSUZU_CORE_ROOT supplies the same control/queue/index/runtime roots as desktop-ingress and is body-free project-bound fail-closed. Verification: focused Codex/Capture/Desktop tests 26 PASS; make check 187 PASS; desktop pnpm test 7 PASS and pnpm build PASS. Cross-surface test proves Tauri draft -> Core receipt/index -> Codex recall, replay/no-self-recall, secret rejection, disabled mode, and project isolation.
close_reason: Codex and Tauri now converge on the selected Core A3/A4 path with verified shared Vault/index, idempotency, guards, and project isolation.

title: iOS Share Extension key lifecycle and live round trip
description:
## Scope
Deliver the mobile-side R4 producer that pairs a device key, stores it in the platform key store, signs a bounded share envelope, and completes one real iOS Share Extension -> Mac TSUZU Core round trip.

## Acceptance criteria
- Pairing establishes a visible key id and revocation path; private key material is not exported as plaintext.
- The Share Extension emits only the documented R4 envelope with expiry, nonce/event id, provenance, and sensitivity metadata.
- A live round trip reaches the desktop verifier/outbox and produces a Core receipt; duplicate, revoked, expired, and offline cases are observable and fail safely.
- The mobile project/release artifact, OS version, signing identity, and test evidence are attached; this repository does not pretend to contain the mobile app if it lives elsewhere.

## Verification
- Mobile unit tests for envelope construction and key lifecycle.
- Desktop integration test consumes the captured fixture from the real extension.
- One physical-device round trip and close/reopen recovery check.

## Boundary
The current TSUZU repository has no native iOS app. This bead is an external deliverable gate that depends on the desktop verifier above, not a reason to add a speculative iOS subtree here.

title: R4 production verifier and paired-key registry
description:
## Scope
Turn the R4 iOS-share protocol from injected signer/verifier callbacks into a concrete desktop-side trust boundary: signed envelope verification, paired-key registration/revocation, replay/expiry checks, and handoff to the existing outbox/CaptureRequest path.

## Acceptance criteria
- A signed share envelope is accepted only for a registered, non-revoked key id, valid schema/version, bounded expiry, and unused nonce/event id.
- Invalid signature, revoked key, replay, expired envelope, tampered payload, and restricted content all fail closed before Canonical mutation.
- Accepted envelopes are persisted through the existing R4 outbox and A3/A4 writer; no direct Canonical write or alternate Vault is introduced.
- Pairing/revocation state is recoverable and included in R5 backup/restore or explicitly excluded with evidence.

## Verification
- Deterministic crypto/protocol tests with golden and fault cases.
- Crash/retry/replay tests around outbox consumption and Core receipt.
- Full Python suite and a local signed-envelope round trip using a generated test key; no production secret is committed.

## Non-goals
This task does not claim that an iOS app or Secure Enclave implementation exists; that is tracked separately. No Claude integration.
notes: 2026-09-23 discovery: R4 v0.2 requires verification against an active paired-device public key but intentionally leaves signature_algorithm as registered_algorithm. Current Python runtime has no cryptography package; system OpenSSL 3.6.2 is available. A concrete algorithm/key-format decision (recommended: Ed25519 SPKI public keys with a tightly bounded local verifier) is required before implementing the production trust boundary; do not substitute test callbacks or symmetric secrets.
